help.title: How it works
help.chart.schedule: Ships leave at 17:00 on day 1. They reach each port by 07:00 and stay at least 8 hours. A ship that would arrive after 11:00 waits for the next morning. Guests must be off by 07:00 on the last morning.
help.chart.fuel: Each leg is sailed as slowly as the schedule allows, never under 10 knots. Burn per mile rises with the square of speed. Lights and galleys burn fuel by the hour. Ports marked with fuel refill the tank.
help.chart.pvsa: A round trip from a US port must call at a foreign port. A cruise can’t start in one US port and end in a different one.
help.chart.ports: A ship too deep or too long for the pier can’t call. Tender ports anchor offshore. They cost a little appeal, and swell can cancel the call.
help.chart.fare: Mass guests shop on price. Premium guests pay more for views and good ports. The best fare is usually where the ship just fills.
help.chart.appeal: Each new port adds its appeal. Each theme adds 2.5. Repeat calls add nothing. Extra sea days on short cruises cost appeal.
help.dd.gm: GM is the gap between the centre of gravity (G) and the point the ship rolls around (M). Weight up high lowers it. Aim for {gm} m or more.
help.dd.list: Uneven weight side to side makes the ship lean. Over 3° is a warning.
help.dd.power: Every room draws power. Generators on the bottom deck supply it.
help.dd.stairs: Every space must be within {reach} cells of a stairwell. Stairwells must stack deck over deck.
help.dd.trial: The trial rolls the ship in a 2.5 m swell. Past 32° it capsizes. A failed trial costs nothing, so test freely.
help.dd.refit: Edit the blueprint of a built ship, pass a trial, then refit. A refit costs 30% of the changed blocks and takes 4 days.
